 State Democratic wins make Medicaid expansion a possibility for more than a million people
 Three of the 10 states that haven’t expanded Medicaid could reconsider their holdout status
 Manage alerts for this article 
 Save this story for later 
 Share this article 
 Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, will seek to expand Medicaid in the state. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images 
 By John Wilkerson 
 Nov. 10, 2026
 John Wilkerson, a Washington correspondent, is the author of D.C. Diagnosis , a twice-weekly newsletter about the politics and policy of health and medicine. 
 John Wilkerson 
 [email protected] John writes about the politics of health care, and he is the author of the twice-weekly D.C. Diagnosis newsletter . You can reach John on Signal at John_Wilkerson.07.
 WASHINGTON — Three of the 10 states that haven’t expanded Medicaid could reconsider their holdout status now that Democrats have secured more power in state government. 
 Texas, Georgia, and Wisconsin are among the states where major power shifts took place in the midterm elections. The Democratic governors-elect in all three made Medicaid expansion a part of their campaigns, though the GOP still holds majorities in part of the state legislatures in Texas and Georgia, which could complicate the path forward. 
 Advertisement
 “Before Tuesday, I would have not expected much activity in the 10 remaining states that have not expanded Medicaid,” KFF Executive Vice President for Health Policy Larry Levitt said, referring to the elections. “But I think that dynamic has changed.”
